source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 3 (ISL A3) · lesson 11. Rewritten for children from Dr. Hassan's lesson; facts and references kept.

title.en: Ramadan: the month of the Qur'an

learn.en: We fast first of all because Allah told us to.
learn.title: Allah commanded it

learn.en: Fasting helps us gain taqwā — keeping Allah in mind so we stay away from wrong. (Qur'an 2:183)
learn.title: To gain taqwā

learn.en: Fasting trains self-control and helps us feel for the hungry, so we become more generous.
learn.title: Strong and kind

learn.en: “The month of Ramadan is the one in which the Qur'an was sent down — guidance for people.” (Qur'an 2:185) So Ramadan is a time to read, listen to and live the Qur'an.
learn.title: The month of the Qur'an

learn.en: “Fasting is a shield.” If someone is rude to a fasting person, he says: “I am fasting.” (Bukhari 1894)
learn.title: A shield

learn.en: “Allah wants ease for you, not hardship.” (Qur'an 2:185) That is why the ill and travellers are allowed to fast later.
learn.title: Allah wants ease

quiz.en: Which book was sent down in Ramadan?
What does a fasting person say if someone is rude to him?
True or false? Fasting is a shield.
True or false? Allah wants hardship for us.

think.q: What could your family do this Ramadan to make it a month of the Qur'an?
think.a: Read a little every day, listen to a reciter in the car, and learn one short verse by heart.

parents.summary: We fast to obey Allah, gain taqwā, train ourselves and feel for the hungry. Ramadan is the month the Qur'an came down. Fasting is a shield.
parents.tip: Plan one page or one short surah a day together in Ramadan.
